title: Phone calls, favors, and “can”
title_target: 可唔可以呀？ — Ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 aa3?
goal: Tell apart four ways to say “can” — 得, 可以, 識, 會 — make a phone call in Cantonese, ask for favors politely, and say no without giving offense.
bekal: tell 得 · 可以 · 識 · 會 apart
make a call: 喂, 搵邊位, 等陣, 覆你
ask for a favor: 唔該, 麻煩你, 可唔可以

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — Calling an office
dialogs.intro: Andi calls Mr. Chan's office. Cantonese phone calls run on set phrases that hardly ever change — learn these six and you can call anywhere in Hong Kong.

lines.speaker: 接線生:
lines.text: [喂|Wai2]，[你好|nei5 hou2]，[新豐公司|San1 fung1 gung1 si1]。
lines.id: Hello, good afternoon, Sun Fung Company.
lines.literal: hello, you — good, San-Fung — company.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [你好|Nei5 hou2]，[唔該|m4 goi1][我搵陳生|ngo5 wan2 Can4 saang1]。
lines.id: Hello, I'd like to speak to Mr. Chan, please.
lines.literal: you — good, please — I — look-for — Chan — sir.

lines.speaker: 接線生:
lines.text: [請問|Cing2 man6][你係邊位呀|nei5 hai6 bin1 wai2 aa3]？
lines.id: May I ask who's calling?
lines.literal: please — ask — you — is — which — classifier — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我姓安|Ngo5 sing3 On1]，[係佢朋友|hai6 keoi5 pang4 jau5]。
lines.id: My surname is On, I'm a friend of his.
lines.literal: I — surnamed — On, am — he — friend.

lines.speaker: 接線生:
lines.text: [等陣|Dang2 zan6]…[唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1]，[佢而家唔喺度|keoi5 ji4 gaa1 m4 hai2 dou6]。
lines.id: One moment… sorry, he's not in right now.
lines.literal: wait — a-moment … sorry, he — now — not — at — place.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [佢幾時返嚟呀|Keoi5 gei2 si4 faan1 lei4 aa3]？
lines.id: What time will he be back?
lines.literal: he — what — time — return — come — huh.

lines.speaker: 接線生:
lines.text: [大概三點|Daai6 koi3 saam1 dim2]。[你要唔要留言呀|Nei5 jiu3 m4 jiu3 lau4 jin4 aa3]？
lines.id: Around three. Would you like to leave a message?
lines.literal: rough — approximate — three — o'clock. you — want — not — want — leave — word — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [唔使喇|M4 sai2 laa3]。[可唔可以|Ho2 m4 ho2 ji5][畀佢電話我呀|bei2 keoi5 din6 waa2 ngo5 aa3]？
lines.id: No need. Could I have his phone number?
lines.literal: not — need — already. can — not — can — give — his — phone — me — huh.

lines.speaker: 接線生:
lines.text: [唔好意思|M4 hou2 ji3 si1]，[我哋唔可以畀|ngo5 dei6 m4 ho2 ji5 bei2]。[但係|Daan6 hai6][我可以幫你留低口訊|ngo5 ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5 lau4 dai1 hau2 seon3]。
lines.id: Sorry, we're not allowed to give it out. But I can take a message for you.
lines.literal: sorry, we — not — can — give. but — I — can — help — you — leave — down — mouth — message.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [咁麻煩你|Gam2 maa4 faan4 nei5]。[話畀佢知|Waa6 bei2 keoi5 zi1][安迪搵過佢|On1 dik1 wan2 gwo3 keoi5]。
lines.id: Then I'll trouble you with that. Please tell him Andi called.
lines.literal: then — trouble — you. say — give — him — know — Andi — look-for — ever — him.

lines.speaker: 接線生:
lines.text: [冇問題|Mou5 man6 tai4]。[仲有咩幫到你呀|Zung6 jau5 me1 bong1 dou2 nei5 aa3]？
lines.id: No problem. Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.literal: not-have — problem. still — have — what — help — able — you — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [冇喇|Mou5 laa3]，[多謝晒|do1 ze6 saai3]。[拜拜|Baai1 baai3]。
lines.id: No, that's all, thanks so much. Bye.
lines.literal: not-have — already, thank — completely. bye — bye.

notes: **On the phone, [搵|wan2] means “I'd like to speak to”.** [我搵陳生|Ngo5 wan2 Can4 saang1] = I'm looking for Mr. Chan. The person answering will say [佢喺度|Keoi5 hai2 dou6] (he's in) or [佢唔喺度|Keoi5 m4 hai2 dou6] (he's not in) — remember 喺度 from Unit 7.
**[你係邊位呀|Nei5 hai6 bin1 wai2 aa3]？ = “who's calling?”** ⚠️ In a formal situation, don't just answer [我係…|Ngo5 hai6 …] plus your first name — give your surname: [我姓安|Ngo5 sing3 On1].

**[留言|lau4 jin4] and [口訊|hau2 seon3] both mean a message left for someone.** [留低口訊|lau4 dai1 hau2 seon3] = to leave a message. [低|dai1] after a verb means “left down there”: [坐低|co5 dai1] (sit down), [寫低|se2 dai1] (write it down).

**[話畀佢知|waa6 bei2 keoi5 zi1] = “let him know”.** ⚠️ The structure is very Cantonese: 話 (say) + 畀 (give) + person + 知 (know). Translating “tell” word for word never produces this sentence; learn it whole.

**[麻煩你|maa4 faan4 nei5] = “sorry to trouble you”.** It's used much like “would you mind…” in English, and is slightly more polite than 唔該. 🇭🇰 For a request that really is a bother, people use both at once: [唔該晒，麻煩你|M4 goi1 saai3, maa4 faan4 nei5].
**[幫到|bong1 dou2] = “able to help”.** The verb + 到 pattern meaning success, like [睇到|tai2 dou2] from Unit 9. [幫唔到你|Bong1 m4 dou2 nei5] = I can't help you — a polite way to say no.
🇭🇰 **Ending a call: [拜拜|baai1 baai3] is enough.** Hanging up abruptly without 拜拜 is considered rude, and some people add [好，就咁先|Hou2, zau6 gam2 sin1] = “OK, that's it for now”.

grammars.title: Four ways to say “can”
body: English uses one word, “can”, for four things that Cantonese keeps strictly apart. Picking the wrong one won't stop you being understood, but it instantly sounds like a translation.

head: Word
Used for
Example
rows: [聽日得唔得呀|Ting1 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3]？ Is tomorrow OK?
[呢度可唔可以泊車呀|Ni1 dou6 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 paak3 ce1 aa3]？ Can I park here?
can because you learned it — a skill
[我識講廣東話|Ngo5 sik1 gong2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2]。 I can speak Cantonese.
[聽日會落雨|Ting1 jat6 wui5 lok6 jyu5]。 It'll rain tomorrow.

head: Negative & question
Form
rows: [唔可以|m4 ho2 ji5] · [可唔可以|ho2 m4 ho2 ji5]？

after: ⚠️ **For skills, Cantonese uses [識|sik1], not 會.** [我識游水|Ngo5 sik1 jau4 seoi2] = I can swim. Mandarin uses 會 there, and Mandarin speakers moving to Cantonese almost always trip up here. 識 also means “to know (someone)”: [我識佢|Ngo5 sik1 keoi5] = I know her.
**In Cantonese, [會|wui5] leans toward the future and likelihood.** [佢會嚟|Keoi5 wui5 lei4] = he'll come. [佢唔會嚟|Keoi5 m4 wui5 lei4] = he won't come. 🔁 You'll use this to talk about plans in Unit 12.

**[得|dak1] is the most versatile and the most Hong Kong of the four.** It can stand alone as an answer: [得|Dak1]！ = sure, OK, will do. [唔得|M4 dak1] = no can do. If you can only remember one of the four, make it this one.

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — Asking a favor and putting off a plan
dialogs.intro: Andi asks Wong Lai for help, then has to change their plans. Two things you'll most often need to do in a foreign language, and both call for politeness.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [黃麗|Wong4 Lai6]，[可唔可以幫我一個忙呀|ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 jat1 go3 mong4 aa3]？
lines.id: Wong Lai, could you do me a favor?
lines.literal: Wong Lai, can — not — can — help — me — one — classifier — busy — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [乜嘢事呀|Mat1 je5 si6 aa3]？[講啦|Gong2 laa1]。
lines.id: What is it? Go ahead.
lines.literal: what — matter — huh. speak — go-on.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我唔識填呢張表|Ngo5 m4 sik1 tin4 ni1 zoeng1 biu2]，[全部係中文|cyun4 bou6 hai6 Zung1 man2]。
lines.id: I can't fill in this form, it's all in Chinese.
lines.literal: I — not — know-how — fill — this — classifier — form, whole — part — is — Chinese — writing.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [冇問題|Mou5 man6 tai4]，[我幫你睇下|ngo5 bong1 nei5 tai2 haa5]。[攞嚟啦|Lo2 lei4 laa1]。
lines.id: No problem, I'll take a look for you. Hand it over.
lines.literal: not-have — problem, I — help — you — look — a-bit. take — come — go-on.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [唔該晒|M4 goi1 saai3]！[仲有|Zung6 jau5]…[唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1]，[星期六|sing1 kei4 luk6][我可能去唔到|ngo5 ho2 nang4 heoi3 m4 dou2]。
lines.id: Thanks so much! Oh, and… sorry, I might not be able to come on Saturday.
lines.literal: thank — completely. still — have … sorry, week — six — I — maybe — go — not — able.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [點解呀|Dim2 gaai2 aa3]？[有嘢做咩|Jau5 je5 zou6 me1]？
lines.id: How come? Something come up?
lines.literal: how — explain — huh. have — thing — do — really.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我老闆叫我返工|Ngo5 lou5 baan2 giu3 ngo5 faan1 gung1]。[真係好對唔住|Zan1 hai6 hou2 deoi3 m4 zyu6]。
lines.id: My boss wants me to go into work. I'm really sorry.
lines.literal: I — boss — tell — me — return — work. really — is — filler — sorry.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [唔緊要啦|M4 gan2 jiu3 laa1]。[咁改星期日得唔得呀|Gam2 goi2 sing1 kei4 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3]？
lines.id: Never mind. How about Sunday instead?
lines.literal: not — important — go-on. then — change — week — day — can — not — can — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [星期日得|Sing1 kei4 jat6 dak1]！[但係|Daan6 hai6][可唔可以遲少少|ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 ci4 siu2 siu2]？[十一點|Sap6 jat1 dim2]？
lines.id: Sunday works! But could we make it a bit later? Eleven?
lines.literal: week — day — can. but — can — not — can — late — little — little. eleven — o'clock.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [得|Dak1]。[我WhatsApp你個地址|Ngo5 WhatsApp nei5 go3 dei6 zi2]。
lines.id: Sure. I'll WhatsApp you the address.
lines.literal: can. I — WhatsApp — you — classifier — address.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [好|Hou2]。[今次|Gam1 ci3][我一定唔會遲到|ngo5 jat1 ding6 m4 wui5 ci4 dou3]！
lines.id: Great. This time I definitely won't be late!
lines.literal: good. this — time — I — surely — not — will — late.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你上次都係咁講|Nei5 soeng6 ci3 dou1 hai6 gam2 gong2][㗎|gaa3]！
lines.id: You said that last time too!
lines.literal: you — last — time — also — is — so — say — emphasis.

notes: **[幫我一個忙|bong1 ngo5 jat1 go3 mong4] = “do me a favor”.** ⚠️ Note the classifier 個 and the word [忙|mong4], which elsewhere means “busy”. It's a fixed phrase; don't take it apart.
**[乜嘢事呀|Mat1 je5 si6 aa3]？ = “what is it?”** The short form [咩事呀|Me1 si6 aa3]？ is the one you'll hear most. [有咩事|jau5 me1 si6] = what's up.

**[我唔識填|ngo5 m4 sik1 tin4] = “I can't fill it in”, because I don't know how.** Compare [我填唔到|ngo5 tin4 m4 dou2] = I couldn't manage to fill it in (something's wrong with the form). Two different kinds of “can't”.
**[可能|ho2 nang4] = maybe.** It goes before the verb: [我可能唔嚟|Ngo5 ho2 nang4 m4 lei4] = I might not come. Other options: [或者|waak6 ze2] (perhaps), [大概|daai6 koi3] (probably).

**[叫|giu3] also means “to tell someone to”.** [老闆叫我返工|Lou5 baan2 giu3 ngo5 faan1 gung1] = the boss told me to go to work. The order: 叫 + person + what they're told to do. Remember 叫 “to be called” from Unit 1 — one character, two roles, and what follows tells them apart.

**[改|goi2] = to change, reschedule.** [改期|goi2 kei4] = change the date; [改時間|goi2 si4 gaan3] = change the time. 🇭🇰 Postponing plans is normal in Hong Kong, as long as you give notice and offer an alternative in the same breath.
**[今次|gam1 ci3] = this time, [上次|soeng6 ci3] = last time, [下次|haa6 ci3] = next time.** The same 今/上/下 pattern as weeks and months in Unit 5.

🇭🇰 **WhatsApp is a verb in Hong Kong.** [我WhatsApp你|Ngo5 WhatsApp nei5] = I'll WhatsApp you. Likewise [我send畀你|Ngo5 send bei2 nei5] and [我call你|Ngo5 call nei5] — Hong Kong Cantonese absorbs whole English words as verbs, and that's completely normal.

grammars.title: Asking for help, saying no, putting things off
body: Three groups of sentences that will save you in real conversations. The polite structure is almost always the same: soft opener → request → reason.

head: Asking
Meaning
Level
rows: [唔該|M4 goi1]，[幫我攞嗰本書|bong1 ngo5 lo2 go2 bun2 syu1]。
[可唔可以幫我一個忙呀|Ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 jat1 go3 mong4 aa3]？
Could you do me a favor?
[麻煩你幫我睇下|Maa4 faan4 nei5 bong1 ngo5 tai2 haa5]。
Would you mind taking a look for me?
[唔知你方唔方便呢|M4 zi1 nei5 fong1 m4 fong1 bin6 ne1]？
I wonder if it would be convenient for you…

head: Declining / postponing
Meaning
rows: [唔好意思|M4 hou2 ji3 si1]，[我今日唔得閒|ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4]。
[我可能去唔到|Ngo5 ho2 nang4 heoi3 m4 dou2]。
I might not be able to make it.
[我幫唔到你|Ngo5 bong1 m4 dou2 nei5]，[真係唔好意思|zan1 hai6 m4 hou2 ji3 si1]。
I can't help you, I'm really sorry.
[改第日得唔得呀|Goi2 dai6 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3]？

after: ⚠️ **Saying no without a reason sounds cold in Hong Kong.** The required pattern: [唔好意思|m4 hou2 ji3 si1] + refusal + reason. The reason can be vague — [我有啲嘢做|ngo5 jau5 di1 je5 zou6] (I've got some things to do) is enough.
**Responding to someone else's refusal: [唔緊要啦|M4 gan2 jiu3 laa1] or [冇所謂|Mou5 so2 wai6].** Both mean “no worries”, and saying it saves face on both sides.
**Thanking someone for help: [唔該晒|M4 goi1 saai3].** Remember the split from Unit 1 — help is a service, so 唔該, not 多謝.

head: Sentence
Meaning
rows: I'd like to speak to Mr. Chan.
[請問你係邊位呀|Cing2 man6 nei5 hai6 bin1 wai2 aa3]？
[我聽唔到|Ngo5 teng1 m4 dou2]，[大聲啲|daai6 seng1 di1]。
I can't hear you, speak up a bit.
I'll get back to you later.
[我而家唔方便講嘢|Ngo5 ji4 gaa1 m4 fong1 bin6 gong2 je5]。
I can't really talk right now.

blocks.title: English words that became Cantonese
items: 🇭🇰 Hong Kong Cantonese absorbs whole English words and treats them as Cantonese. This isn't slang; it's how people talk every day, including at the office.
[call你|call nei5] call you · [send畀你|send bei2 nei5] send to you · [book枱|book toi2] book a table · [check下|check haa5] check quickly
[cancel咗|cancel zo2] canceled · [confirm返|confirm faan1] reconfirm · [OK啦|OK laa1] OK then · [sorry呀|sorry aa3] sorry

**Notice that the Cantonese markers still go on**: [cancel咗|cancel zo2] uses 咗 from Unit 9, [send畀你|send bei2 nei5] uses 畀 from Unit 2. The English word slots into Cantonese grammar, not the other way round.

sections.title: 識 vs 得: a drill to tell them apart

blocks.text: These two get mixed up most. The rule is simple: [識|sik1] is about **you** — something you've mastered. [得|dak1] is about **circumstances** — whether the situation allows it.

head: Sentence
Meaning
Why
rows: [我識講廣東話|Ngo5 sik1 gong2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2]。
[我唔識游水|Ngo5 m4 sik1 jau4 seoi2]。
[聽日得唔得呀|Ting1 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3]？
[呢度可唔可以食嘢呀|Ni1 dou6 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 sik6 je5 aa3]？
[聽日會落雨|Ting1 jat6 wui5 lok6 jyu5]。

blocks.title: Four sentences every beginner needs
items: [我識少少廣東話|Ngo5 sik1 siu2 siu2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2]。 — I speak a little Cantonese.
[唔該講慢啲|M4 goi1 gong2 maan6 di1]。 — Please speak a bit more slowly.
[我唔明|Ngo5 m4 ming4]，[可唔可以再講一次呀|ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 zoi3 gong2 jat1 ci3 aa3]？ — I don't understand, could you say that again?
[呢個廣東話點講呀|Ni1 go3 Gwong2 dung1 waa2 dim2 gong2 aa3]？ — How do you say this in Cantonese? — the sentence that will grow your vocabulary fastest.

items: [我會講廣東話|Ngo5 wui5 gong2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2]。

[我唔可以游水|Ngo5 m4 ho2 ji5 jau4 seoi2]。 (meaning: can't swim)

answers: 識 — 得 … 得 — 可以 … 可以 — 會 — 識 — 會
可唔可以幫我一個忙呀？ — 麻煩你幫我睇下。 — 唔該講慢啲。 — 可唔可以再講一次呀？ — 唔好意思，我今日唔得閒。
喂 唔該 我 搵 陳生 — 佢 而家 唔 喺 度 — 話 畀 佢 知 安迪 搵 過 佢 — 我 可能 去 唔 到 — 改 星期日 得 唔 得 呀 — 我 幫 唔 到 你
May I ask who's calling? — I can take a message for you. — I don't know how to fill in this form. — I can't really talk right now. — You said that last time too!
Ngo5 sik1 siu2 siu2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2. — Ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 bong1 ngo5 jat1 go3 mong4 aa3? — M4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 gam1 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4. — M4 goi1 gong2 maan6 di1. — Goi2 dai6 jat6 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3?
Ngo5 sik1 gong2 Gwong2 dung1 waa2. — Ngo5 ting1 jat6 dak1. — Ngo5 waa6 bei2 keoi5 zi1. — M4 hou2 ji3 si1, ngo5 m4 dak1 haan4. — Ngo5 m4 sik1 jau4 seoi2.
wave: Five minutes before Unit 11: call yourself. Say an entire phone conversation out loud, from 喂 to 拜拜, playing both roles — caller and receiver. Then put together three requests for help you genuinely need this week, each with a soft opener, the request and a reason. Sentences you actually need stick much faster than example sentences.
